Order 
This is first bail application under Section 483 of BNSS filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 07.09.2025 by Police Station Raghogarh, District Guna in connection with Crime No.201/2025, registered in relation to the offence punishable under Section 75(1)(I) of the BNS, Sections 376(3), 372(2)(n) of the IPC and Section 5(L)/6 & 17 of the POCSO Act.

As per prosecution story, the complainant, who knew Vinod Thakur (present applicant) for approximately two years from her coaching classes at Sada, submitted a written application dated 13.06.2025 alleging that on 21.05.2025, while returning home alone by bus from Padarkhedi to Sada Colony, when she got down at Sada Chowk around 8:00 PM and was walking home that near her residence, Vinod Thakur (applicant) met her, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24724 2 MCRC-43554-2025 grabbed her right hand with wrongful intent, and attempted to take her to a hotel, but she resisted, freed herself, and proceeded home.
Frightened by the incident, she did not immediately report it.
On 13.06.2025, she informed her father and grandfather and lodged a complaint at the police station.
Alleged FIR bearing Crime No.201/2025 under Section 75(1)(i) of B.N.S. was registered, and investigation commenced.

sentences.text: Based on evidence, Sections 376(3), 376(2)(n), and 506 IPC were added, and as the complainant was a minor, Sections 5L/6 of the POCSO Act were invoked.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He has not committed any offence.
It is further submitted that the allegations leveled against the applicant are entirely false, baseless, and have been concocted to malign his reputation.
The applicant has no connection with the alleged incident.
It is further submitted that the complainant did not report the matter immediately.

The alleged incident occurred on 21.05.2025, whereas the complaint was lodged only on 13.06.2025, resulting in a delay of nearly three weeks, which casts serious doubt on the credibility of the allegations.

It is further submitted that at the time of the alleged offence mentioned in the FIR, the prosecutrix was major, but to falsely implicate the applicant in serious offences, a fabricated story, allegedly of 2-3 years prior, has been narrated in the prosecutrix's statement with the apparent intention to harass the applicant and tarnish his reputation.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24724 3 MCRC-43554-2025 During the Section 183 statement
, the prosecutrix appears to have attempted to fill gaps in the story, allegedly under family pressure and undue influence.
It is further submitted that the narrative given by the prosecutrix in her Section 183 statement is nothing but a product of undue influence and fear of her father.
No act was ever committed by the applicant that would constitute the alleged enhanced sections of the IPC or the POCSO Act.
It is further submitted that there is no direct evidence linking the applicant to the alleged offence and mere suspicion or uncorroborated statements cannot justify custodial detention.
The medical and forensic reports, including DNA tests, are yet to conclusively implicate the applicant.
He is in custody since 07.09.2025.
Trial will take time for its conclusion.
The applicant is permanent resident of District Guna and there is no likelihood of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
He is ready to abide by the terms and conditions as may be imposed.
With the aforesaid submissions, prayer for grant of bail is made out.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that the trial is not likely to conclude in near future and prolonged pre- trial detention being an anathema to the concept of liberty, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.

Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24724 4 MCRC-43554-2025 solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court for his appearance on the dates given by the concerned Court subject to compliance of the following conditions by the applicant:-
